correctness.rationale: The proof gives an exact if-and-only-if. Extreme sufficiency follows by a descending/ascending block cascade under the k-propagation rule; necessity follows from the inability to enter an unselected open-neighborhood twin class larger than k and from the initial stall created by selecting a nonextreme class larger than k. An extreme A_p,B_1 pair dominates the graph, proving the universal upper bound two. A direct implementation exhaustively confirms the formula for 4092 canonical profiles through order 11 and k=1,2,3,4; this finite check is supplementary, not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The invariant is a standard network-monitoring parameter that is hard on broad bipartite classes. Chain graphs are a natural hereditary nested-neighborhood subclass. The theorem completely determines generalized k-power domination for every k>=1 by two canonical block-load maxima, gives explicit one-vertex witnesses and a universal two-vertex fallback, and yields a linear-time test from the canonical decomposition. This is a structural classification rather than a routine substitution or arbitrary finite computation.
